data.name: Guyana
data.summary: Guyana taxes residents on worldwide income at 25% and 35% (35% above GYD 3,360,000 in 2026). Capital gains on assets held over 12 months bear a separate 20% capital gains tax, but gains on shares in public companies are exempt (whether this covers foreign listed shares is unconfirmed). Dividends from Guyanese companies are exempt; foreign dividends are ordinary income. No inheritance, estate, gift or wealth tax, and individuals have been exempt from property tax since 2025.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Worldwide income tax at 25%/35%; separate 20% capital gains tax; no inheritance, gift or wealth taxes.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if present more than 183 days in a year, residing permanently, or intending to reside permanently (PwC Residence).

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains tax of 20% applies to net gains from a change of ownership of assets by an individual; gains on assets disposed of within 12 months are taxed as income (up to 35%). Gains on the disposal of shares in public companies are exempt. A private residence is exempt if the proceeds are reinvested in another residence.

capital_gains.rate_basis: PwC Other taxes: 20% CGT on net gains (assets held over 12 months); exemption for shares in public companies (applied to Guyanese listed shares). Unlisted company shares and local real estate: 20%.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trading gains are business income at 25%/35%.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: Assets disposed of within 12 months: gain taxed as income at 25%/35%.

dividends.summary: Dividends paid by resident companies to resident individuals are exempt. Foreign dividends are part of worldwide income taxed at 25% and 35% (top rate above GYD 3,360,000 chargeable income in 2026). Foreign tax credit is provided for income from an office, employment or profits and under treaties (Canada, UK, CARICOM, UAE).

dividends.rate_basis: Top PIT rate 35% (2026 threshold GYD 3,360,000) on foreign dividends; domestic dividends exempt (PwC Income determination).
dividends.withholding_outbound: 20% WHT on dividends to non-residents (treaty: Canada 15%, UK 10%, CARICOM 0%).
dividends.treaty_network: Treaties only with Canada, UK, UAE and CARICOM states.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax; individuals are exempt from property tax from 2025.

succession.name: Guyana
succession.summary: A will is largely free, but a court can order provision for a spouse, children and other dependants from the estate under the Family and Dependants Provision Act. Succession follows the common-law domicile rules and no choice of foreign law is given. Guyana has common-law trusts but is not in the Hague Trusts Convention, and no private-foundation law was found.
succession.family_claims: The Family and Dependants Provision Act (Act 22 of 1990, as amended by Act 10 of 2012) lets a court order maintenance or provision for qualifying family and dependants out of the net estate, including where a will omits them.
succession.foreign_law_note: Common-law rule (not confirmed in a Guyanese statute here): movables pass under the law of the deceased's domicile and land under the law of its location. No right to choose the law of nationality was found.
succession.trust_note: Common-law trusts are available (Guyana is a common-law country). Guyana is not a party to the Hague Trusts Convention. No private foundation law was found; charities are handled through other statutes. The family-provision Act has anti-avoidance rules that may reach assets moved out of the estate.
open_questions: Chapter number of the Family and Dependants Provision Act is cited as 12:22 by the Ministry of Legal Affairs file and as 12:24 elsewhere; confirm.
Who qualifies as an applicant, the time limit, and whether trust assets fall in the net estate were not read.
Whether Guyana has a trust statute (beyond the common law and the Trustees Act) and whether foundations exist was not verified.
Domicile and conflict rules for succession were not sourced in a Guyanese statute or case.
